title: DEVELOPMENT OF AN ELECTRO-DYNAMIC SHIELD SYSTEM FOR PLANETARY MISSIONS EXPRO+
description: Objective: To develop an Electro-Dynamic-Shield system to mitigate systems degradation for missions to the Moon, Mars and planetarybodies including a significant dusty environment.Description: Exploration systems in contact with planetary surfaces covered in regolith such as the Moon and Mars are subject to local dust displacement and accumulation on critical surfaces affecting system performance as for instance thermal balance, power generation efficiency and optical transmission and system lifetime. A number of mitigation strategies have been put forward and tested mostly on ground with a very limited demonstration in space. The Electro-Dynamic Shield (EDS) technology is a method used to mitigate the accumulation of dust on surfaces, particularly in space environments. This technology employs electric fields to repel dust particles, preventing them from settling on critical surfaces such as solar panels, sensors, and other equipment. This technology has been studied for more than twenty years outside of Europe for the mitigation of dust deposition on terrestrial and space system and it has been recently demonstrated on the Moon. In Europe, most of the studies performed so far have been on laboratory scale. Among others, an experimental EDS was successfully implemented on a number of samples including optical glass and Kapton sheets and demonstrated very high dust removal efficiency in a vacuum environment including UV, showing good potential for targeted system feasibility studies. Based on this success, the feasibility of implementing such technology on actual space hardware by breadboarding and testing critical functionalities can be addressed. This activity encompasses the following tasks: - Define the requirements for the implementation of an EDS system into relevant spacecraft structures and materials of interest with a priority towards solar arrays (with possible applicability to optical surface and other materials) and define the requirements from the target system towards EDS. - Assess the required modifications of standard designs to accommodate an EDS system, establish a list of technological gaps, define specific tests and a test plan to address the technological gaps. - Design and manufacture relevant breadboards to demonstrate EDS operational efficiency on targeted system. - Perform test for critical functionalities,including in representative laboratory environments (dusty vacuum and in presence of UV). - Based on the tests outcomes and future missions needs provide a technical roadmap with a cost outline.

title: Ireland – Construction work – Metrolink vehicle safety features for all construction and logistics activity involving HGV usage during the programme.
description: Metrolink vehicle safety features for all construction and logistics activity involving HGV usage during the programme: • M100 – Advance Works (Land access and clearance, Archaeology, Utilities, environmental monitoring and sewer alignment works). • M300 – Enabling Works (Glasnevin Station, O’Connell Street Station Box, Irish Rail Glasnevin Interface and ESBN HV MV connections). • M400 - Main Civils Works – (M401 Civil Works Southern Section, M402 Civil Works Northern Section). • M500 – DBFOM (Public Private Partnership) for station fit-out, provision of rolling stock and rail systems, commissioning and operation of passenger services. Metrolink will require extensive deployment of Heavy Goods Vehicles (HGVs of all types from 3.5T to >12T) to support a wide range of activities, including deliveries, disposal and site servicing. Given the scale of operations, it is essential to ensure vehicle compliance with the European Union General Safety Regulations (EU GSR) from July 2024. A significant proportion of the HGV fleet in Ireland does not meet these standards, primarily due to manufacture and registration dates prior to July 2024. Although there is no national legal requirement to retrofit legacy vehicles within the Irish fleet, deploying large numbers of HGVs that are not fitted with the latest vehicle safety technology represents a significant hazard to vulnerable road users (both workforce and the general public). This presents an unacceptable risk to the programme which seeks a zero-tolerance approach to vehicle safety, to protect vulnerable road users both on and off various construction sites, zones and public roads. Metrolink and Transport Infrastructure Ireland (TII) have identified three key vehicle safety systems that must be adopted on HGVs in use across the programme, to significantly reduce risks to vulnerable road users and improve overall safety across project sites: • Reversing Detection (RD) • Blind Side Information Systems (BSIS) • Moving Off Information Systems (MOIS) EU Regulation 2019/2144, the General Safety Regulation (GSR), sets mandatory standards for vehicle safety by requiring new vehicles to have advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS) and meet specific performance criteria. From 2024 all new HGV (N2/N3) must have the following fitted as standard: • Intelligent Speed Assistance • Blind Spot Information System • Advanced Emergency Breaking System • Reversing Detection • Moving Off Information System • Tyre Pressure Monitoring System • Alcohol Interlock Installation Facilitation • Driver Drowsiness and Attention Warning

title: Paikkatieto- ja ympäristötietojärjestelmät palveluna
description: Hankinnan kohteena on paikkatieto- ja ympäristötietojärjestelmät palveluna. Paikkatietojärjestelmä tarjoaa selainpohjaisen karttapalvelu -sovelluksen, jossa näytetään kohteiden sijainteja ja ominaisuustietoja käyttäjille. Paikkatietojärjestelmä sisältää tarvittavat aineistot, kuten taustakartat ja kiinteistötiedot. Järjestelmä tukee paikkatiedon tarkastelua, hakua, analysointia ja paikkatietokohteiden muokkaamista. Ympäristötietojärjestelmä vastaanottaa paikkatietoon sidottua ympäristödataa, jota voidaan analysoida ja raportoida sekä julkaista paikkatietojärjestelmän tai erillisen ympäristöpalveluiden paikkatietosovelluksen kautta. Tarkoituksena on tuottaa ympäristötietoa ja paikkatietoa yhdistävää tilannekuvaa, esimerkiksi teemakarttojen muodossa, sekä mahdollistaa ympäristönsuojelua koskevan tiedon hallinta ja ajantasaisen tilannekuvan ylläpito. Keskeistä hallittavaa tietoa ovat ympäristötarkkailun ja vesihuollon analyysitulokset. Käyttäjien näkökulmasta erityisesti tilannekuvan tarkastelun ja raportoinnin tuottamisen tulee olla helppoa ja järjestelmän tulee sisältää hyvät hakutoiminnallisuudet. Hankintaan sisältyy: - järjestelmien kehitys ja testaaminen- järjestelmien mahdollisesti vaatimat maksulliset käyttöoikeudet- järjestelmien käyttöönotto ja integraatiot - järjestelmien tuki- ja ylläpitopalvelut, sekä- järjestelmien ja niiden käyttöön liittyvät asiantuntijapalvelut sekä mahdollinen jatkokehitys.
